political: DJ Kim: first transfer to opposition 1997; three peaceful transfers; Lee Myung-bak and Park Geun-hye both prosecuted post-office; Yoon Suk-yeol martial law declaration December 3 2024 — most acute democratic stress test since 1987; National Assembly vote removing martial law within hours
external: North Korea: permanent existential threat providing military justification for state; US alliance as security anchor; China: largest trade partner vs US alliance tension; Japan: historical grievance + security alignment; THAAD deployment as China-US proxy conflict
unique_aspects: Yoon December 2024 martial law is the most acute democratic stress test of any consolidating democracy in the dataset — a sitting president declared martial law at 10pm, the National Assembly voted it down by 190-0 at 1am, and it was lifted by 4am. Fastest democratic self-correction in the library. Park Geun-hye impeachment + Yoon reversal: two major institutional stress tests passed within 8 years. South Korea is the strongest Asian control case.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; Korea Democracy Barometer; National Election Commission; Yoon martial law December 2024 — data still incoming

econ_conditions: Asian financial crisis 1997–98: rupiah lost 80% value, Suharto 32yr regime collapsed within months; Reformasi economic restructuring + IMF conditionality; commodity export economy (palm oil, coal, nickel) creating resource dependency; Jokowi infrastructure-led growth; 2024: Prabowo government — son of Suharto as VP (Gibran)
social: World's largest Muslim majority democracy — Islam and democracy compatibility as global demonstration case; 270m people, 17,000 islands, 700+ languages — governance complexity unmatched; decentralisation creating local strongman politics (bossism); 1998 anti-Chinese riots as ethnic violence warning
institutional: 1998–2002 constitutional amendments: direct presidential election, term limits, civilian military control, Constitutional Court created; KPK anti-corruption commission — later weakened by Jokowi 2019; Mahkamah Konstitusi (Constitutional Court) ruling on Gibran eligibility (Jokowi's son) enabling dynastic politics
political: Reformasi coalition fracturing into patronage networks; SBY era: democratic consolidation + anti-corruption; Jokowi: popular outsider → dynasty builder (Gibran as VP); Prabowo 2024 victory — former military general accused of 1998 abductions; democratic quality declining without formal breakdown
external: ASEAN membership providing regional legitimacy norm; China: Belt and Road investment + South China Sea tension; US: democratic ally + strategic partner; Australia: security partner; IMF structural adjustment conditioning 1998–2000 transition
unique_aspects: Largest Muslim-majority democracy in world — the global demonstration case for Islam-democracy compatibility. Transition triggered entirely by economic crisis (1997 Asian financial crisis) rather than political mobilisation — the most economically-determined transition in the library. Jokowi-Gibran dynastic politics using Constitutional Court manipulation to enable son's candidacy is new mechanism: judicial capture serving dynastic not partisan consolidation. Prabowo 2024 — a man accused of ordering 1998 disappearances winning democratic election.
data_notes: V-Dem 1945–2024; SMRC/Indikator polling; KPU election data; ANFREL monitoring; note Suharto period coded separately

econ_conditions: Garment industry ($40bn export) as economic foundation — workers as political constituency; Hasina: genuine economic growth (7%+ GDP) providing legitimacy; 2022 energy crisis + inflation eroding living standards; Yunus caretaker government: IMF negotiations + anti-corruption drive
social: Student protest movement (Anti-Discrimination Movement) July–August 2024 — triggered by quota system for 1971 liberation war descendants; Gen Z digital mobilisation unprecedented in South Asia; Hasina fled August 5 2024 after army withdrew support; 400+ killed in 6 weeks of protests
institutional: Awami League captured election commission, judiciary, civil service over 15 years; 2014 and 2018 elections neither free nor fair; BNP (main opposition) systematically suppressed; army as ultimate veto player — withdrew support August 5 triggering collapse; Muhammad Yunus interim government from August 2024
political: Hasina: daughter of independence leader — legitimacy from liberation war founding myth; BNP (Khaleda Zia) as main opposition; two-family political duopoly (Hasina/Zia) for 30 years; quota protests spreading beyond quota issue to full regime rejection within 3 weeks; speed of collapse unmatched in modern dataset
external: India: strategic ally backing Hasina — Modi relationship; China: Belt and Road investment; US: democracy concerns vs strategic interests; Yunus: Nobel laureate, international legitimacy enabling rapid recognition; IMF: conditionality supporting reform government
unique_aspects: Fastest regime collapse in the modern dataset — from student protests to prime minister fleeing in 6 weeks. First regime in library ended primarily by Gen Z digital mobilisation (TikTok/Facebook coordination). The quota protests began as a specific policy grievance and became a general anti-regime movement within days — shows how rapidly single-issue protests can generalise in high-repression contexts. First female authoritarian leader removed in the library — adds gender dimension previously absent. Army withdrawal of support as the decisive mechanism rather than institutional vote or election.
data_notes: V-Dem 2000–2024; Daily Star Bangladesh; Prothom Alo; August 2024 events still being coded; ANFREL election monitoring

econ_conditions: Crony capitalism: Marcos-linked oligarchs controlling major industries; martial law justified by communist threat + economic development; 1983 Aquino assassination triggering capital flight and economic crisis; IMF bailout 1984; economy contracting 7% 1984–85 — collapse precursor
social: People Power Revolution February 1986 — 2 million in EDSA highway; Catholic Church (Cardinal Sin) as civil society organiser; Ninoy Aquino assassination 1983 as galvanising event; middle class joining anti-Marcos coalition; military reform movement (RAM) creating elite fracture
institutional: Martial law 1972 suspending constitution; 1973 constitution enabling Marcos indefinite rule; Batasang Pambansa as rubber stamp; Comelec captured; snap election 1986 — Marcos declaring victory despite Corazon Aquino winning; NAMFREL parallel count showing Aquino winning
political: Snap election triggered by US pressure (Reagan administration); NAMFREL (civil society parallel count) as new mechanism; military defection (Enrile/Ramos) triggering People Power; Marcos exile to Hawaii — US-managed exit; Aquino transition internationally supported
external: US: Cold War anti-communist ally → democracy pressure post-Aquino assassination; Reagan administration: Reagan-Marcos relationship personal; Marcos exile to Hawaii US-facilitated; IMF conditionality; Catholic Church international connections
unique_aspects: People Power Revolution is the original template for mass civic mobilisation removing an authoritarian. The NAMFREL parallel vote count (1986) is the first documented case of civil society parallel vote tabulation — precursor to Venezuela 2024 actas. Military defection (Enrile/Ramos joining People Power) as mechanism: authoritarian collapse requires elite fracture, not just mass mobilisation. Catholic Church mobilisation as specific to Catholic-majority societies — Filipino, Polish, Chilean parallels.
data_notes: V-Dem 1945–2024; NAMFREL documentation; Ateneo de Manila election studies; Teresa Encarnacion Tadem research

econ_conditions: Duterte: populist infrastructure spending + drug war; Marcos Jr.: son of dictator winning via social media nostalgia campaign; Chinese investment as alternative to US; economic growth maintained despite authoritarian drift; Sara Duterte as VP then falling out — coalition fracture 2024
social: Drug war: 6,000–30,000 killed extrajudicially — state violence at scale; social media disinformation (Marcos rehabilitation narrative on TikTok/Facebook) as primary tool; millennial voters with no Marcos dictatorship memory; Sara Duterte-Marcos Jr. falling out creating unusual coalition breakdown
institutional: ICC investigation into drug war killings — Philippines withdrew from ICC 2019; Supreme Court: some independence maintained; Commission on Elections: functional but under pressure; ABS-CBN broadcast network closure 2020 as media capture; Anti-Terrorism Act 2020
political: Duterte 2016: anti-establishment outsider + brutal drug war + China pivot; Marcos Jr. 2022: 31m votes (largest in Philippine history) on nostalgia + social media rehabilitation; Leni Robredo as opposition — losing but maintaining democratic opposition viability; Sara Duterte VP then impeachment threat 2024
external: US: traditional ally + ICC tension + Marcos rehabilitation problematic; China: South China Sea disputes intensifying under Marcos Jr. (pivot back to US); ICC: withdrew but investigation continues; diaspora (10m overseas Filipinos) as political constituency
unique_aspects: Nostalgia authoritarianism: the son of the dictator whose removal was a global democracy milestone winning the largest electoral victory in Philippine history via TikTok rehabilitation campaign. No historical parallel for a dictator's direct heir democratically winning 31 years after People Power. Social media as historical revisionism tool operating at scale. Sara Duterte coalition breakdown (VP threatening to assassinate president) is constitutionally unprecedented.
data_notes: V-Dem 2000–2024; PULSE Asia surveys; COMELEC data; PCIJ investigative journalism; ICC preliminary examination documents

econ_conditions: IMF dependency: 23 IMF programmes since 1958 — most in Asia; military budget ~4% GDP regardless of civilian/military government; remittances from Gulf diaspora ~$30bn/yr as stabilising factor; China CPEC ($60bn) creating new patron dependency; 2022–23 IMF crisis + inflation spike
social: Islam as constitutional framework (Islamic Republic) + secular military tradition tension; Pashtun/Punjabi/Sindhi/Baloch ethnic federalism under permanent stress; Ahmadiyya persecution as constitutional discrimination; Imran Khan: first leader with mass urban youth base (PTI); blasphemy law as social control mechanism
institutional: Military as 'deep state': ISI controlling foreign policy, strategic industries, media; Supreme Court: occasional independence (Musharraf removal 2007 lawyers movement); National Accountability Bureau as political weapon; 18th Amendment 2010: significant civilian powers — then military circumventing
political: 4 direct coups (1958/1969/1977/1999); Zulfikar Ali Bhutto executed; Benazir Bhutto assassinated; Imran Khan: 2018 won with military support → 2022 no-confidence removal → 2024 jailed + election manipulation; PTI winning 2024 election while leader in jail — unique
external: US: Cold War ally + War on Terror + democracy pressure tension; China: CPEC + all-weather friendship; India: Kashmir permanent conflict; Afghanistan: Taliban border dynamic; Saudi Arabia/Gulf: financial support + religious influence; nuclear arsenal as ultimate constraint
unique_aspects: Nuclear-armed cyclical democracy — the only nuclear state in the dataset with genuine alternation between military and civilian rule. Imran Khan 2024: first case of a party winning parliamentary elections while its leader is in jail and its candidates forced to run as independents — and still winning. The military as the permanent constitutional actor operating outside the constitution is the defining structural feature. 23 IMF programmes demonstrates that economic crisis alone cannot force democratic consolidation.
data_notes: V-Dem 1947–2024; PILDAT democracy assessment; IRI Pakistan surveys; note military periods require separate coding

leader: Min Aung Hlaing / Aung San Suu Kyi
econ_conditions: Military (Tatmadaw) controlling 40%+ of economy via MEHL and MEC conglomerates; jade/gems + timber + gas as military revenue independent of civilian budget; 2021 coup: GDP -18% 2021; sanctions + capital flight; PDG (resistance) controlling territory with parallel economic administration
social: 135 officially recognised ethnic groups — ethnic armed organisations as permanent political actors; Rohingya genocide 2017 — Suu Kyi defending military internationally; Buddhist nationalist movement (MaBaTha) as political tool; 2021 coup: civil disobedience movement + generation Z resistance
institutional: 2008 constitution: 25% military seats in parliament (requiring 75%+ for constitutional change — designed as veto); NLD winning 2015 and 2020 supermajorities; State Counsellor role created for Suu Kyi (constitutionally barred from presidency); 2021 coup reversing entire transition
political: Suu Kyi: 30yr opposition icon → Nobel Peace Prize → government leader → military prisoner; 2020 election: NLD won 83% of seats — military claiming fraud; February 2021 coup on eve of new parliament; NUG (National Unity Government) formed in exile; PDG armed resistance controlling significant territory by 2024
external: China: largest investor + coup non-condemnation + blocking UNSC action; ASEAN: non-interference principle preventing meaningful response; US/EU: sanctions + NUG recognition; India: border + gas pipeline pragmatism; Thailand: refugee flows + trade
unique_aspects: Military that never truly transferred power — the 2008 constitution's 25% military seats was a veto design, not a transition mechanism. Suu Kyi defending military at ICJ over Rohingya genocide then imprisoned by same military is a unique reversal of extraordinary symbolic power. PDG (People's Defence Force) resistance controlling more territory than any resistance movement in the dataset — potentially the largest armed democracy movement in history. China's role as coup enabler via UNSC veto is the clearest modern case of external authoritarian support.
data_notes: V-Dem 1948–2024; data quality declining post-2021; Fortify Rights; AAPP political prisoner documentation; NUG parallel governance data

econ_conditions: Tourism-dependent economy (20% GDP pre-COVID) creating vulnerability to political instability; Thaksin rural development programmes buying northern/northeastern loyalty; Military budget increasing post-2014 coup; Chinese investment as alternative patron; 2017 constitution designed to prevent Thaksin-aligned majority governing
social: Red Shirt (pro-Thaksin, rural north/northeast) vs Yellow Shirt (urban elite/royalist) as permanent fracture; lèse-majesté law: up to 15 years prison for royal criticism; Move Forward/People's Party: youth urban anti-establishment movement; Pita Limjaroenrat: won plurality 2023, barred from government
institutional: Constitutional Court: dissolved Thai Rak Thai (2007), PPP (2008), Future Forward (2020), Move Forward (2024); 2017 constitution: appointed Senate blocking any non-military-approved government; NACC anti-corruption used selectively; Election Commission composition determining election results
political: Thaksin family winning every free election since 2001; 2006 coup → judicial coup 2008 → 2010 crackdown (90 dead) → 2014 coup → 2023 Move Forward winning plurality → coalition blocked → Move Forward dissolved → Pheu Thai (Thaksin) forming coalition with military parties; Thaksin returned from exile 2023
external: US: traditional ally with military relationships; China: growing economic influence + political model appeal to military; ASEAN: non-interference; Thaksin: Dubai exile + international business networks; monarchy: Thai king residing in Germany — unusual
unique_aspects: 22-year cycle with no resolution — neither democratic consolidation nor authoritarian consolidation achieved. Constitutional Court as primary political weapon: dissolved 4 political parties including the most popular party (Move Forward, 14m votes) in 15 years. The monarchy as invisible veto player operating through judicial and military proxies has no direct parallel. Thaksin's 2023 return from exile while Pheu Thai forms coalition with coup-makers who ousted him is historically extraordinary — pragmatic accommodation across the divide that defined Thai politics for 20 years.
data_notes: V-Dem 1945–2024; ANFREL monitoring; iLaw constitutional monitoring; King Prajadhipok Institute democracy surveys

econ_conditions: UMNO developmental state: NEP affirmative action for Malays creating race-based economic distribution; 1MDB scandal ($4.5bn stolen) as crystallising corruption event; Mahathir 1997 Asian crisis: capital controls vs IMF — unorthodox worked; post-2018 coalition instability affecting investment; Anwar: reformist economics vs race-religion pressures
social: Malay Muslim majority (60%) vs Chinese (23%) vs Indian (7%) as permanent ethnic political framework; NEP affirmative action creating inter-ethnic tension; Reformasi movement (Anwar Ibrahim imprisonment 1998) as civil society foundation; GE14 2018: historic first BN defeat after 61 years
institutional: UMNO 61-year dominance via gerrymandering + malapportionment + sedition law; Judiciary: independence partially maintained (Anwar acquittal 2004); MACC anti-corruption: activated for Najib (unprecedented) then Najib jailed 2022; 2018 transition: UMNO accepting loss — critical institutional moment
political: Mahathir (UMNO founder) returning aged 92 to lead opposition coalition defeating UMNO 2018 — unique; Sheraton Move 2020: backdoor government collapsing elected coalition; Muhyiddin/Ismail Sabri instability; Anwar Ibrahim: 24yr opposition journey finally PM 2022; UMNO coalition partner with former enemy
external: China: largest trade partner + BRI investment; US: traditional security partner; Singapore: economic integration + water treaty; ASEAN founding member; OIC: Islamic solidarity dimension; 1MDB: Goldman Sachs settlement showing US legal reach
unique_aspects: 61-year single party dominance peacefully ended via election — rarer than it sounds. Mahathir's return at 92 to defeat the party he built over 60 years earlier is without parallel in democratic history. The Sheraton Move (2020 backdoor government) demonstrates that electoral victory does not guarantee power in a system with fluid party loyalties. Anwar Ibrahim's 24-year journey from deputy PM → sodomy conviction → opposition leader → PM is the longest democratic rehabilitation arc in the dataset.
data_notes: V-Dem 1957–2024; Merdeka Center polling; BERSIH election monitoring; Malay Mail; note Sabah/Sarawak as separate political entities

econ_conditions: $18tr GDP (2nd largest) — economic power enabling authoritarian independence from external pressure; Belt and Road Initiative as authoritarian influence export ($1tr+ committed); COVID zero-COVID policy economic cost; Xi's anti-corruption campaign eliminating rivals under economic justification; real estate crisis (Evergrande) as first major internal economic threat
social: Xi Jinping Thought as mandatory ideology; Uyghur mass detention (1m+) in Xinjiang — largest internment since WWII; Hong Kong National Security Law 2020 ending one country two systems; COVID zero-COVID protest (white paper movement) November 2022 — rare public dissent; social credit system expansion
institutional: Collective leadership norm (9-member PSC) → Xi centralisation; term limits removed 2018 — constitutionally; CMC (military) under Xi personal control; CPPCC and NPC as legitimating facades; discipline inspection commission (CCDI) as anti-corruption/purge instrument
political: Anti-corruption campaign: 1.5m officials punished — genuine reform + rival elimination; Belt and Road as foreign policy instrument; Wolf Warrior diplomacy replacing Deng Xiaoping's 'hide and bide'; Taiwan pressure increasing; no succession mechanism visible; COVID handling as legitimacy test
external: US: comprehensive strategic competition; Taiwan: reunification timeline pressure; Russia: no-limits partnership + Ukraine war complexity; EU: systemic rival; Global South: development financing creating political influence; nuclear arsenal: second-strike capability
unique_aspects: Pure authoritarian deepening within a system that never had competitive elections — cannot be compared to backsliding cases. Scale (1.4bn people) makes this unique in the dataset. Xi's removal of term limits is constitutionally distinct from other cases: the norm was informal (established by Deng), not constitutional — its removal required changing the constitution rather than circumventing it. Belt and Road as authoritarian influence export is a new phenomenon: no previous authoritarian in the library had the economic capacity to systematically export its governance model.
data_notes: V-Dem 1949–2024; note expert survey quality declining post-2015 due to researcher intimidation; HRIC; Congressional-Executive Commission on China

leader: Goh Chok Tong / Lee Hsien Loong / Lawrence Wong
econ_conditions: GDP per capita $65k+ (among highest globally); sovereign wealth funds (GIC + Temasek) ~$1.5tr; financial hub + biotech + digital economy transition; COVID management: one of world's most effective; cost of living crisis as first significant domestic legitimacy challenge
social: Founding generation PAP leaders dying (Lee Kuan Yew 2015); 4G leadership (Lawrence Wong) less personally authoritative; pink dot LGBTQ+ movement — 377A repeal 2022 as social liberalisation; opposition Workers' Party holding 10 seats (most ever) after 2020 election; social media enabling opposition coordination despite media control
institutional: GRC system: group representation constituencies forcing ethnic slates — structural opposition barrier; ISA (Internal Security Act): last used for terrorism, not politics recently; defamation law: still used but less frequently; POFMA (Protection from Online Falsehoods) 2019 — new digital censorship tool; elected presidency: Tony Tan / Halimah Yacob (reserved election) as legitimacy questions
political: Lee Hsien Loong 20yr PM tenure ending 2024 (Lawrence Wong succession); Workers' Party: first credible opposition in 55 years; 2020 election: PAP 61% (lowest since independence) but retained supermajority; Halimah Yacob walkover presidency 2017 — only Malay candidate allowed to contest; POFMA creating chilling effect
external: US: security partner + democratic pressure; China: ethnic Chinese majority + economic integration tension; Malaysia: water treaty + Johor-Singapore dependency; ASEAN: founding member + host of secretariat; global financial flows: BVI/Cayman alternative + Russian oligarch assets post-2022
unique_aspects: The central question: can the Singapore model survive the death of its founding generation? Lee Kuan Yew's personal authority was irreplaceable. Lawrence Wong has none of the biographical legitimacy that justified authoritarian control. Workers' Party holding 10 seats is the beginning of genuine political competition — the first time in 55 years the system faces real pressure from within electoral rules. POFMA (fake news law) is a new digital authoritarianism tool without precedent in the historical library.
data_notes: V-Dem 1965–2024; IPS (Institute of Policy Studies) surveys; Elections Department; Kirsten Han / New Naratif independent journalism

econ_conditions: Rajapaksa family economic mismanagement: tax cuts 2019 + organic farming ban 2021 + Chinese debt + COVID tourism collapse = $51bn external debt default 2022; foreign currency reserves depleted (couldn't import fuel/medicine); IMF bailout negotiated; NPP (Dissanayake) 2024: debt restructuring + anti-corruption platform
social: Aragalaya protest movement April–July 2022: largest in Sri Lankan history; storming of presidential palace July 9 2022 as iconic moment; Gotabaya Rajapaksa fleeing to Maldives then Singapore; economic hardship (queues for fuel/gas for months) as mobilising condition; Tamil-Sinhalese ethnic tension as permanent background variable
institutional: Presidential system enabling Rajapaksa family concentration; Parliament functioning — forced Rajapaksa resignation; Supreme Court: some independence (ruled Rajapaksa policies unconstitutional); 2024 presidential election: Dissanayake (NPP/JVP) first left government since independence
political: Rajapaksa dynasty: Mahinda (president) + Gotabaya (president) + Basil (finance minister) + Chamal (speaker) — unprecedented family control; Gotabaya fled, Wickremesinghe elected by parliament as caretaker; 2024: Dissanayake NPP won on anti-corruption + accountability platform — genuine democratic accountability
external: China: Hambantota port ($1.4bn) as debt trap model debate; India: emergency financial support during crisis; IMF: $2.9bn programme conditioning reforms; US: democracy support; Maldives + Singapore: hosting fleeing president
unique_aspects: Economic collapse as democracy-saving mechanism — the Rajapaksa family's mismanagement was so severe it generated mass mobilisation that removed them before they could consolidate fully. Contrast Venezuela: oil wealth enabled consolidation despite economic damage; Sri Lanka had no oil buffer. The storming of the presidential swimming pool (July 9 2022) as symbol: ordinary citizens literally swimming in the president's pool while he fled. First left government in Sri Lankan history elected in 2024 — demonstrates democratic accountability functioning even after extreme institutional stress.
data_notes: V-Dem 1948–2024; CPA election monitoring; Verité Research; note Tamil minority coding requires attention

econ_conditions: UNTAC elections 1993 creating nominal democracy; garment industry ($10bn) as economic base with worker suppression; Chinese investment dominant (40%+ FDI); Hun Sen: controlling economic patronage through CPP networks; 2023: economy dependent on China making external democratic pressure ineffective
social: Khmer Rouge trauma (2m dead, 25% of population) as permanent social memory; FUNCINPEC royalist constituency absorbed or suppressed; CNRP (opposition) dissolved 2017; civil society NGOs operating under foreign agent-style pressure; 2023: Candlelight Party (CNRP successor) prevented from registering
institutional: UNTAC-established institutions captured within 10 years; 1997 coup: Hun Sen ousting Ranariddh via violence; Sam Rainsy opposition operating from exile; Supreme Court dissolving CNRP 2017; NEC election commission fully CPP-controlled; 2023 election: CPP won 120/125 seats with main opposition barred
political: Hun Sen: 38 years as PM (1985–2023) — third longest in world; 2023 transition to son Hun Manet — authoritarian dynastic succession; CNRP dissolved on terrorism charges; Kem Sokha imprisoned; Sam Rainsy in exile; Cambodian diaspora as opposition voice
external: China: primary patron replacing US post-2017; ASEAN: non-interference protecting Hun Sen; US: democracy funding cut + sanctions on Hun Sen associates; EU: EBA (Everything But Arms) trade preferences suspended 2020; UN: UNTAC legacy creating ongoing accountability pressure
unique_aspects: UN-administered elections (UNTAC 1993) producing democracy that was then systematically dismantled over 30 years — the longest-running case of gradual post-UN-transition consolidation in the dataset. Hun Sen to Hun Manet: first authoritarian dynasty transfer in Southeast Asia via planned succession rather than coup or election. China's role as replacement patron (after US withdrew funding) is the clearest case of authoritarian patron substitution enabling consolidation.
data_notes: V-Dem 1953–2024; LICADHO human rights documentation; COMFREL election monitoring; Radio Free Asia

status: Completed transition — partial backsliding then recovery
econ_conditions: Apartheid economy: dual structure (first world white + third world black); BEE (Black Economic Empowerment) creating black middle class but also connected elite; Zuma era state capture: Gupta family controlling cabinet appointments and SOE contracts; Eskom collapse (load shedding 10–12hrs/day) as governance failure metric; 32% unemployment structural — highest in dataset
social: Rainbow Nation narrative vs reality of persistent racial inequality; Gini coefficient 0.63 — highest in dataset; xenophobia against other African migrants (2008, 2015, 2019 waves); land expropriation debate as permanent political fault line; ANC as liberation movement losing moral authority under Zuma; Fees Must Fall 2015–16 as generational mobilisation
institutional: Constitutional Court as strongest institution — Zuma jailed for contempt 2021 (unique: sitting ex-president jailed); Public Protector office captured under Busisiwe Mkhwebane then restored under Kholeka Gcaleka; NPA (prosecutorial service) captured then recovering; Electoral Commission (IEC) maintaining independence throughout; Section 89 impeachment process functioning
political: Mandela: 1 term deliberately — institutional norm-setting; Mbeki: Aids denialism as governance failure; Polokwane 2007: Zuma defeating Mbeki in ANC internal election; state capture 2009–2018: systematic looting of SOEs (Transnet, Eskom, SAA); Ramaphosa: reform project vs ANC factional resistance; 2024 election: ANC below 50% for first time — GNU (Government of National Unity) with DA
external: BRICS membership creating China/Russia alignment tension with Western partners; AU leadership role — Ramaphosa Ukraine mediation; IMF: no programme but fiscal consolidation pressure; investor confidence as constraint on policy; Mozambique/Zimbabwe instability as regional spillover
unique_aspects: Constitutional Court jailing a former president for contempt of court — the only case in the entire library of an institution successfully holding a former head of government legally accountable post-office without foreign pressure. The 2024 GNU (ANC + DA + IFP) is unprecedented: liberation movement governing with its historic white-minority-party opponent. State capture fully documented (Zondo Commission: 5,000+ pages) providing the richest institutional corruption dataset in the library.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; Afrobarometer; ISS (Institute for Security Studies); Zondo Commission report; Electoral Commission IEC data

leader: Rawlings → Kufuor → Mills → Mahama → Akufo-Addo → Mahama
econ_conditions: Cocoa + gold export economy; 2007 oil discovery (Jubilee field) — resource curse risk managed better than most; 2022 debt crisis: IMF programme after debt default — democratic institutions surviving economic stress; NDC-NPP alternation creating policy uncertainty but institutional stability; remittances 6% GDP
social: Two-party system (NDC-NPP) with genuine competition; Akan cultural majority but ethnic coalition building required; chieftaincy as parallel governance structure (600+ paramount chiefs); strong civil society (Ghana Civil Society Platform); media freedom index: consistently best in West Africa; religious tolerance (Christian-Muslim roughly equal)
institutional: Electoral Commission (EC): consistently credible — 2020 disputed result resolved without violence; Supreme Court: 2013 election petition (Mahama vs Akufo-Addo) heard and decided — loser accepted; CHRAJ (human rights commission) functioning; Auditor-General exposing corruption; Parliament: genuine debate and oversight
political: Rawlings: military ruler converting to democratic politician — unique trajectory; NDC-NPP alternation 1992–2026: 5 peaceful transfers; 2008 election decided by 40,000 votes — accepted; 2020 EC announcement contested but Supreme Court petition filed (not streets); Mahama returning 2024 — second non-consecutive term
external: ECOWAS leadership role — Ghana hosting multiple regional institutions; IMF: 2022 programme as economic anchor; World Bank: consistent development partner; China: infrastructure investment; US: AGOA trade preferences; AU: Ghana as stability model cited repeatedly
unique_aspects: Africa's most important control case — 5 peaceful electoral transfers in a region where the average is less than 1. The 2013 Supreme Court election petition is the cleanest example of democratic dispute resolution in the African dataset: loser took dispute to court, court ruled, loser accepted. The 2022 debt crisis and IMF programme is a critical stress test — economic catastrophe that did not produce democratic backsliding. Ghana disproves the 'Africa cannot consolidate democracy' thesis most directly.
data_notes: V-Dem 1957–2024; Ghana Statistical Service; Electoral Commission; Afrobarometer; CDD-Ghana; Supreme Court 2013 petition documentation

econ_conditions: Oil dependency: 90% of exports, 60% of government revenue — resource curse operating; Dutch disease hollowing manufacturing; 2016 recession (-1.6%) first in 25 years — oil price driven; naira devaluation and fuel subsidy removal 2023 creating inflation shock; 200m population with 40% in extreme poverty despite oil wealth; Lagos as parallel economic universe ($100bn GDP — larger than most African countries)
social: 250+ ethnic groups — Hausa-Fulani (north) + Yoruba (southwest) + Igbo (southeast) as dominant tripartite; Boko Haram insurgency (30,000+ dead, 2m displaced) as permanent security variable; #EndSARS 2020 — youth protest against police brutality shot by army (Lekki Toll Gate); Niger Delta militancy as oil infrastructure threat; 2023 election: youth turnout record but results disputed
institutional: INEC (electoral commission): 2015 Jonathan conceding before result announced — watershed moment; Supreme Court: 2023 Tinubu election petition — upheld despite evidence questions; EFCC (anti-corruption): selective enforcement; NNPC (oil company) opacity; military: professional but political influence persisting; state governors as semi-autonomous power centres
political: Jonathan 2015 concession — first sitting African president to concede electoral defeat by phone call to opponent; Buhari: ex-military ruler returning as democrat — legitimacy experiment; 2023: Tinubu ('emilokan' — it is my turn) controversial victory; LP Obi candidacy: youth mobilisation crossing ethnic lines for first time; INEC BVAS technology improving but implementation contested
external: ECOWAS leadership — Nigeria as regional hegemon (60% of West African GDP); Sahel coups creating regional instability; China: largest bilateral creditor; UK: diaspora (900,000) + historical relationship; US: security cooperation + democracy promotion tension; IMF: no programme but Article IV consultations
unique_aspects: Africa's largest democracy (100m+ registered voters) surviving Boko Haram insurgency, oil price crashes, ethnic fragmentation, and serial electoral disputes without democratic collapse. Jonathan's 2015 concession is the single most important democratic act in African political history — changed the continental calculus. #EndSARS and Lekki Toll Gate: army firing on unarmed protesters at a toll booth is the kind of event that ends regimes in the dataset — Nigeria survived it. Scale makes this uniquely important: if Nigeria fails democratically, it affects more people than any other African case.
data_notes: V-Dem 1960–2024; Afrobarometer; SBM Intelligence; INEC data; 2023 election petition Supreme Court records; Stears data

econ_conditions: From Africa's breadbasket to 500bn% hyperinflation (2008) — most extreme economic collapse in peacetime democratic dataset; Fast Track Land Reform 2000: white farm seizures destroying agricultural exports; ZIM dollar abandoned 2009; USD economy then RTGS$ then ZIG; 80% informal economy; Mnangagwa: dollarization + Chinese investment + diamond revenue opacity
social: ZANU-PF liberation war legitimacy as founding political currency; Gukurahundi: 20,000 Ndebele killed 1983–87 — Mnangagwa implicated; MDC (Tsvangirai) as opposition surviving systematic violence; 2008 election: Tsvangirai winning first round then withdrawing due to violence (200+ supporters killed); brain drain: 4m Zimbabweans in South Africa
institutional: ZEC (electoral commission): systematically captured; judiciary: initially independent then packed (Chidyausiku court); CIO (Central Intelligence Organisation) as political repression tool; security sector: ZANU-PF's private army; November 2017 military intervention removing Mugabe — not a coup officially; ConCourt: 2018 Chamisa petition dismissed in 24 hours
political: Mugabe: independence hero → 37-year authoritarian; 2000 referendum defeat — first signal of weakness; MDC formation as genuine opposition threatening ZANU-PF for first time; GNU 2009–2013 (ZANU-PF + MDC forced coalition) as unique African power-sharing; Mnangagwa coup-not-coup: 'assisted transition' establishing military as permanent kingmaker; 2023 election: SADC observer mission unprecedented criticism
external: South Africa: quiet diplomacy (Mbeki) failing to pressure Mugabe; SADC: non-interference norm protecting Mugabe; China: all-weather friend + infrastructure investment + military equipment; UK: land reform as colonial guilt variable; AU: Mugabe respected as liberation elder; sanctions (US ZIDERA, EU) limited effectiveness
unique_aspects: Hyperinflation of 500 billion percent — the most extreme economic mismanagement of any country in the dataset that did not produce immediate regime collapse. Mugabe lasting 10 years after economic catastrophe demonstrates liberation movement legitimacy as extraordinary resilience factor for authoritarian regimes. The 2017 'military-assisted transition' is a new category: not a coup (no shots fired, Mugabe negotiated out) but not constitutional — creating a precedent copied in Sudan and Mali.
data_notes: V-Dem 1980–2024; Zimbabwe Human Rights NGO Forum; ZHRC; Afrobarometer; SADC observer mission reports; GNU documentation

econ_conditions: Genocide left GDP -50% in 1994; Vision 2020/2050: fastest-growing African economy 7–8% annually; Kigali as Africa's cleanest city — governance as brand; services + tourism + tech hub strategy; coffee and tea exports; no oil — forced to build competitive economy; inequality: high Gini despite growth (0.43)
social: Post-genocide reconciliation: gacaca courts processing 1.9m cases; Hutu-Tutsi identity officially banned — 'Rwandan' only; women 61% of parliament (highest globally); monthly umuganda community work mandatory; tight social control: no street protests, no critical media; RPF surveillance described as pervasive by dissidents
institutional: Parliament: highest female representation globally but rubber stamp; Supreme Court: packed; National Electoral Commission: captured; RPF party = state; Local governance (imihigo performance contracts) as accountability mechanism downward; Diaspora engagement structured through RPF networks
political: Kagame: RPF military commander who ended genocide → president since 2000; 2003 referendum + 2015 referendum enabling indefinite rule; Paul Rusesabagina (Hotel Rwanda hero) imprisoned 2020 — international outcry; Victoire Ingabire imprisoned; 2024 election: Kagame 99.15%; no viable opposition permitted
external: France: genocide complicity → reconciliation 2021; DRC: Rwanda accused of supporting M23 rebels (UN reports); Uganda: periodic tensions; UK: Rwanda asylum deal (2022–24) creating unusual bilateral relationship; AU: Kagame as respected voice on African development; ICC: not a member
unique_aspects: Post-genocide reconstruction creating unique legitimacy basis unavailable to any other authoritarian in the library — the regime literally saved the country from extinction. This makes standard democratic backsliding analysis almost inapplicable: what is the counterfactual? Singapore is the only comparable case of genuine competence + systematic political control, but Singapore never faced genocide. The gender parity (61% women in parliament) coexisting with zero political freedom is analytically paradoxical.
data_notes: V-Dem 1990–2024; Human Rights Watch; Amnesty International; gacaca documentation (NURC); expert survey quality limited by access constraints

econ_conditions: Second most populous African country (120m) — scale creating unique governance complexity; EPRDF developmental state: 10% growth 2004–2018 — Africa's fastest; Abiy liberalisation: foreign investment surge 2018–2019; Tigray war 2020–2022: $28bn economic damage, 500,000+ dead (UN estimate); Tigray + Amhara conflicts ongoing — fiscal strain; IMF programme 2023
social: 80+ ethnic groups under ethnic federalism (kilil system); EPRDF: Tigrayan minority (6%) dominating coalition despite Oromo (35%) majority; Abiy: first Oromo PM — euphoria of 2018; OLA (Oromo Liberation Army) insurgency continuing post-peace; Amhara Fano militia as new armed actor; Eritrean troops in Tigray — rape and atrocities documented by UN
institutional: EPRDF: four ethnic parties (TPLF, ODP, ADP, SEPDM) forced to merge into Prosperity Party — TPLF refused; National Electoral Board: first credible election attempt 2021 but Tigray excluded; judiciary: insufficient independence; Abiy consolidating: NEBE, security services, military under personal control; federal structure surviving but strained
political: TPLF (Tigray People's Liberation Front): dominated Ethiopia 1991–2018; Abiy Nobel Peace Prize 2019 — fastest from reform hero to war criminal accusation; November 2020 Tigray war start: Abiy framing as law enforcement operation; Pretoria Peace Agreement November 2022; 2021 election: Prosperity Party landslide but legitimacy contested; Amhara conflict 2023 — new front opening
external: Eritrea: Isaias Afwerki as Abiy ally against TPLF — Eritrean troops committing atrocities in Tigray; Somalia: ATMIS mission; Egypt: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) as Nile water conflict; AU: Pretoria mediation; UN/OCHA: humanitarian access denied to Tigray; US: sanctions threat + AGOA suspension
unique_aspects: The most dramatic reversal of a democratic opening in the African dataset — Nobel Peace Prize winner launching a war that produced 500,000+ dead within 18 months of the award. The ethnic federalism system (designed to manage diversity) becoming the fault line along which the state nearly fractured. Eritrean troop involvement (foreign military fighting inside Ethiopia against Ethiopian citizens) has no parallel in the dataset. The GERD (dam) as a potential trigger for interstate war between Ethiopia, Egypt, and Sudan adds a unique regional dimension.
data_notes: V-Dem 1991–2024; ACLED conflict data; UN OCHA; Ethiopian Human Rights Commission; expert survey access limited during conflict

econ_conditions: Francophone West African economy — CFA franc monetary union; phosphate + groundnuts + fishing; 2014 oil/gas discovery (offshore) — resource curse risk emerging; 2021–24 Sall: attempting constitutional manipulation while managing oil transition; Faye 2024: new generation economic agenda; 40% poverty rate despite growth
social: Sufi brotherhoods (Mouridiyya, Tijaniyya) as parallel social organisation — marabouts as political brokers; Wolof cultural dominance without ethnic conflict; Casamance separatism (low-level 40yr insurgency) as ongoing pressure; strong civil society (Y'en a Marre movement); vibrant press; French language creating elite-mass gap
institutional: Constitutional Council: ruled against Sall's third term attempt 2024 — critical institutional resistance; National Assembly: Sonko's Pastef party winning majority; High Court of Justice: functional; CENA (election commission) with moderate independence; Sall's attempt to postpone election February 2024: Constitutional Council overruling him
political: Diouf: peaceful transfer to opposition (Wade) 2000 — first in West Africa; Wade: democratic entry then third-term attempt blocked by protests (2012); Sall: two terms then attempting postponement — blocked by Constitutional Council; March 2024: Faye (Sonko ally) winning — Sall accepted result; Ousmane Sonko: opposition leader imprisoned then released then PM
external: France: CFA franc + military bases + Françafrique relationships; ECOWAS: Senegal as stability anchor in coup-affected region; IMF: programme + oil sector governance advice; EU: migration partnership (illegal departures to Canaries); USA: PEPFAR + security cooperation
unique_aspects: Africa's most important resilience demonstration of 2024 — Constitutional Council blocking presidential election postponement, forcing Sall to hold elections he appeared to want to avoid, and Faye winning. Three consecutive peaceful transfers (Diouf→Wade→Sall→Faye) makes Senegal unique in Francophone Africa. The Sufi brotherhood system as parallel governance is analytically unique — marabouts commanding bloc votes and providing social services outside the state.
data_notes: V-Dem 1960–2024; Afrobarometer; CENA; Constitutional Council rulings; Y'en a Marre documentation

leader: Bashir → TMC → Hamdok → SAC → civil war
econ_conditions: Oil exports lost when South Sudan seceded 2011 (75% of revenue); inflation 300%+ by 2019 triggering uprising; bread price doubling as immediate protest trigger; gold mining under SAF/RSF parallel control — war financing; 2023 civil war: economy effectively collapsed; 10m+ displaced — largest displacement crisis globally
social: December 2018 uprising: bread prices → 'freedom, peace, justice'; Sudanese Professionals Association (SPA) organising — doctors, lawyers, engineers as vanguard; women's leadership (kandakas) prominent; April 2019 sit-in outside military HQ — largest in Sudanese history; RSF (Rapid Support Forces) descending from Janjaweed (Darfur genocide perpetrators) as military actor
institutional: TMC (Transitional Military Council) after Bashir removal; Sovereignty Council (military + civilian) as hybrid; Constitutional Declaration August 2019; October 2021 coup: Burhan removing civilian partners; parallel command structures (SAF + RSF) as institutional time bomb; April 2023: SAF-RSF war starting in Khartoum
political: Bashir 30yr regime: ICC arrest warrant (Darfur genocide) — first sitting head of state indicted; 2019 uprising removing Bashir — mass mobilisation success; Hamdok as civilian PM: civilian-military power sharing; 2021 coup: Burhan and Hemedti (RSF) removing civilian government; April 2023: Burhan vs Hemedti war — two generals who executed 2021 coup turning on each other
external: UAE: supporting RSF (Hemedti) — gold trade; Saudi Arabia: supporting SAF (Burhan); Egypt: supporting SAF; Russia: Wagner presence + gold concessions; Ethiopia: Pretoria process; AU: suspended Sudan; US: sanctions + attempted mediation (Jeddah talks); ICC: Bashir warrant unexecuted
unique_aspects: The only case in the dataset where a successful mass protest movement removing an authoritarian (2019) led to civil war between the two military factions who initially managed the transition. The SAF-RSF war is analytically unique: two parallel military structures created during the Bashir era as mutual deterrents (so neither could coup alone) turning on each other. The Janjaweed-to-RSF transformation (genocide militia → national paramilitary → coup co-conspirator → belligerent) is the most complete institutional corruption arc in the library.
data_notes: V-Dem 1956–2024; ACLED; Sudan Conflict Observatory; OCHA humanitarian data; SPA documentation; post-2023 data quality severely limited

econ_conditions: Landlocked — gold exports + subsistence agriculture; French colonial CFA franc system; 2012 coup context: Tuareg rebellion + jihadist expansion destroying northern economy; French military (Barkhane) costs without economic benefit; junta era: France expelled + Wagner/AES arrival; gold revenue under junta control; 2023 ECOWAS sanctions on Niger ($30bn GDP impact)
social: Tuareg identity (nomadic, trans-border) as permanent structural fault line; Peul/Fulani communities caught between jihadists and army — atrocity allegations against both; French language creating elite-mass gap; Islam: Sufi traditional vs Salafi-jihadist competition; youth bulge (65% under 25) + 30% unemployment as mobilisation base
institutional: 2012 coup: Captain Sanogo removing Touré — ECOWAS forcing transition; IBK (Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta) elected 2013 legitimately; M5-RFP protest movement 2020; August 2020 coup; second coup March 2021; junta CNSP → transition → CNSP again; Burkina Faso: two coups 2022; Niger: coup July 2023; AES (Alliance des États du Sahel) as anti-ECOWAS bloc
political: Domino effect: Mali 2020+2021 → Guinea 2021 → Burkina 2022+2022 → Niger 2023 — 6 coups in 3 years in the region; anti-French sentiment as genuine popular base (not just junta PR); Wagner Group arrival as Russian geopolitical tool; ECOWAS sanctions failing to restore democracy; junta transitional timelines consistently extended
external: France: Barkhane → expelled from Mali, Burkina, Niger; Russia/Wagner: filling security vacuum + gold concessions; Algeria: border + diplomatic mediation; Mauritania: relative stability as regional contrast; AU: suspended all three + Guinea; ECOWAS: sanctions + threat of military intervention (Niger) not executed; US: reducing footprint
unique_aspects: The first regional democratic collapse — 6 coups in 3 years across a contiguous geographic zone represents a new systemic phenomenon not seen since Latin America in the 1960s-70s. The anti-French sentiment is genuine mass politics, not just junta manipulation — creating democratic legitimacy for anti-democratic actors. Wagner Group as a new external actor type: private military company providing security in exchange for mining concessions, without the diplomatic constraints of state actors. AES (Mali+Burkina+Niger) forming a new regional bloc specifically to escape ECOWAS democratic conditionality — new institutional architecture of authoritarianism.
data_notes: V-Dem 1960–2024; ACLED; Armed Conflict Survey; ISS West Africa; ECOWAS documentation; Wagner presence: ACLED + investigative journalism

econ_conditions: Diamond wealth (De Beers partnership) managed unusually well — Debswana model: government 50% partner; Botswana Development Corporation as sovereign wealth mechanism; GDP per capita: $100 (1966) → $8,000 (2026) — fastest sustained growth in world history 1966–2000; 2023: Moody's upgrade; diversification challenge as diamonds depleting; 20% unemployment structural
social: Tswana cultural majority (80%) without meaningful ethnic conflict — unique in African context; San (Bushmen) minority rights as ongoing question; HIV/AIDS: 25% prevalence peak 2000 → managed down to 12% via universal treatment programme; strong civic culture; low corruption perception (Africa's least corrupt consistently); Kgotla (traditional assembly) as participatory governance
institutional: Independent Electoral Commission: credible since 1969; High Court: genuine independence; Directorate on Corruption and Economic Crime (DCEC): functional; Ombudsman; Parliament: genuine debates; 2023: IEC managing first competitive transfer in 57 years cleanly; BCP (Duma Boko) accepting result immediately
political: BDP (Botswana Democratic Party): 57yr dominance without becoming authoritarian — the puzzle the Singapore comparison highlights; Seretse Khama founding legitimacy; 2019: Masisi defeating Khama (former president backing opposition) — internal BDP conflict; 2023 election: BDP losing to UDC (Duma Boko) — first transfer; Khama in exile in South Africa during 2019–2023
external: South Africa: economic dependency (80% trade) + SACU customs union; De Beers/Anglo American: diamond partnership; UK: Commonwealth relationship; Zimbabwe: refugee flows; Namibia: Chobe water sharing; no significant security threats enabling domestic consolidation focus
unique_aspects: Diamond wealth managed for development rather than capture — the resource curse not operating. 57 years of single-party democracy without authoritarian consolidation — the longest in Africa. The 2023 transfer is the completion of the arc: the system produced a genuine alternation after 57 years, demonstrating that long dominant-party democracies can self-correct electorally. The Kgotla system (traditional public meetings for community decision-making) as participatory governance predating colonialism and surviving into modern democracy.
data_notes: V-Dem 1966–2024; Afrobarometer; IEC Botswana; Transparency International (consistently top 3 in Africa); Statistics Botswana

econ_conditions: East Africa's largest economy — Nairobi as regional hub; mobile money (M-Pesa) as financial innovation; flower exports + tourism + tea; 2007–08 post-election violence cost $1bn; 2022 drought + global inflation creating 2023 Gen Z protest context; IMF programme 2023; debt: 70% GDP
social: 42 ethnic groups — Kikuyu-Luo rivalry as dominant fault line (Kenyatta-Odinga dynasties); 2007–08: 1,300 killed in post-election ethnic violence — ICC cases; Nusu Mkate (half-bread) coalition as forced power-sharing; Gen Z protests June–July 2024 (finance bill) — new non-ethnic youth mobilisation; Odinga-Ruto handshake 2018 as conflict resolution model
institutional: IEBC (election commission): 2017 Supreme Court nullifying election — unique globally; 2022 IEBC: credible result accepted by Odinga; Supreme Court: demonstrated genuine independence (2017 nullification); ICC cases: Kenyatta and Ruto charged then cases collapsed — impunity concern; EACC anti-corruption: limited effectiveness
political: Moi 24yr authoritarian → 2002 peaceful transfer (NARC coalition); Kibaki-Raila 2007 disputed → violence → Kofi Annan mediation → GNU; 2013/2017 Jubilee (Kenyatta-Ruto); 2017 Supreme Court nullification globally unique; 2022: Ruto defeating Odinga — Odinga finally accepting result; 2024 Gen Z protests forcing Ruto to withdraw finance bill and reshuffle cabinet
external: EAC membership; IMF: programme + conditionality; US: security partnership (counterterrorism); China: SGR railway ($3.6bn) + debt controversy; UK: historical relationship; Somalia: Al-Shabaab spillover as security variable; ICC: withdrawal attempt failed
unique_aspects: 2017 Supreme Court nullifying a presidential election is the only case in the entire dataset of a court overturning a sitting president's re-election — globally unprecedented. The 2024 Gen Z protest movement (finance bill) is analytically significant: non-ethnic, social-media organised, crossing class lines — fundamentally different from historical Kenyan mobilisation. The Odinga-Ruto handshake (political enemies becoming allies) as conflict prevention mechanism is the most used political tool in East Africa — now a model.
data_notes: V-Dem 1963–2024; KNBS; IEBC; Supreme Court 2017 nullification records; Afrobarometer; KNCHR post-election violence documentation

econ_conditions: Abolished army 1948 — defence budget redirected to education and health; eco-tourism + tech sector (Intel, Amazon) as modern economy; dollarized services economy; 2009 fiscal crisis managed without democratic stress; 5% GDP growth average; relatively low inequality by LatAm standards (Gini 0.48); universal healthcare (Caja) as social contract anchor
social: "Pura vida" cultural identity as genuine political consensus; strong environmental consciousness; universal literacy (97%) highest in LatAm; no indigenous land rights resolution as ongoing tension; migration: 400,000 Nicaraguan migrants creating labour market politics; evangelical church growth challenging Catholic social consensus
institutional: Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE): the most trusted electoral institution in Latin America — decisions accepted by all parties since 1949; constitutional ban on re-election (one term only) eliminating incumbency advantage; Sala IV (Constitutional Chamber) as genuinely independent court; Defensoría de los Habitantes (ombudsman) functioning; Contraloría General auditing state
political: PLN-PUSC two-party system → fragmentation post-2014; PAC outsider Solís winning 2014; Carlos Alvarado 2018 on marriage equality platform — won; Rodrigo Chaves 2022: populist outsider winning but within institutional constraints; no serious coup attempt in 76 years; one-term limit preventing personality consolidation
external: OAS founding member; CAFTA (Central America Free Trade Agreement) with US; regional destabilisation pressure (Nicaragua, Honduras); Panama as economic partner; no military alliance needed — no army; climate leadership disproportionate to size
unique_aspects: The only country in the dataset that abolished its army and has maintained unbroken democracy for 76 years — these two facts are causally connected. The TSE (electoral tribunal) is the single most trusted electoral institution in the entire library — its decisions have never been seriously contested by a losing party. One-term presidential limit as the most effective single institutional innovation against personalismo. The most important control case for testing what enables democratic consolidation without military backing.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; TSE election data; LAPOP; Latinobarómetro; 76 years of unbroken electoral data — highest quality in LatAm

econ_conditions: Welfare state model unusual in LatAm — Batllismo legacy; 2002 banking crisis (-11% GDP) survived democratically; Frente Amplio (left) governing 2005–2020 without democratic regression; social policies: marijuana legalisation, same-sex marriage, abortion rights — progressive without instability; 2020 Lacalle Pou (right) winning — peaceful transfer; low Gini (0.39) by LatAm standards
social: Most secular society in Latin America — church separation 1919; strong labour movement (PIT-CNT); university autonomy tradition; 95% literacy; small population (3.5m) enabling social cohesion; Tupamaro guerrilla movement (1960s–70s) integrating into democratic politics as MPP — unique rehabilitation
institutional: Electoral Court: independent and trusted; Parliament: genuine legislative power; Supreme Court: functioning independence; Frente Amplio: left coalition proving democratic left can govern without institutional capture; Ministerio Público: anti-corruption functioning; INDDHH human rights institution
political: Military dictatorship 1973–1985: pacted transition via Naval Club Agreement; Sanguinetti first democratic president; Frente Amplio winning 2005 (Tabaré Vázquez) — first left government; Mujica (2010–2015): most admired LatAm president of era; FA-PC-PN alternation functioning; Orsi (FA) winning 2024 — third left government
external: Mercosur founding member; strong rule-of-law reputation attracting investment; ICSID arbitration record: Uruguay winning tobacco case against Philip Morris; OAS active participant; Argentina economic crises creating spillover risk; Brazil political instability as contrast
unique_aspects: Tupamaro guerrillas (who kidnapped diplomats and robbed banks in the 1970s) becoming a governing political party (MPP) and producing President Mujica — the most complete transformation of an armed movement into democratic politics in the dataset. The only LatAm country that successfully resisted tobacco industry legal pressure (Philip Morris ICSID case) — rule of law functioning against a multinational. Mujica donating 90% of presidential salary to charity and living on a farm — symbolic politics with genuine democratic legitimacy effect.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; Corte Electoral; LAPOP; Latinobarómetro; Mujica presidency extensively documented

econ_conditions: Oil at $140/barrel (2008) enabling Misiones social programmes; GDP contraction 75% between 2013–2021 — worst peacetime economic collapse in hemisphere; hyperinflation 1,000,000% in 2018; parallel exchange rate as corruption mechanism; PDVSA purge after 2002 strike converting oil company to political instrument; US sanctions accelerating collapse while strengthening nationalist narrative
social: 7 million emigrants (25% of population) — largest displacement crisis in Western hemisphere; Colectivos: armed pro-regime civilian militias replacing police; malnutrition and healthcare collapse creating humanitarian emergency; elite emigration preceding mass emigration — early warning signal confirmed; Chavismo as identity not just politics — barrio base remains loyal
institutional: 1999 Constitution: Chávez rewrote rules via referendum; Supreme Court packed with chavistas after 2004 recall referendum; Electoral Council (CNE) fully captured — no credible elections since 2013; National Assembly bypassed via Supreme Court 2017; 2024 election: Maduro claiming victory, opposition producing cryptographic proof of fraud (actas)
political: Coup attempt 2002: Chávez survived, radicalised consolidation; oil strike 2002–03: Chávez won, purged PDVSA; 2004 recall referendum: won, demoralised opposition; Maduro succession: chavismo without Chávez losing legitimacy rapidly; 2019 Guaidó parallel presidency — institutional dual power; 2024: Edmundo González winning per parallel count, Maduro refusing to leave
external: Cuba: intelligence and security apparatus training; US: 2002 coup support then sanctions; ALBA as counter-US regional bloc; Russia/China: oil-for-loans financing regime survival; Colombia: spillover + Petro attempting mediation; Carter Center withdrawing from 2024 observation
unique_aspects: Only modern case reaching full collapse endpoint while remaining nominally sovereign — useful because the full arc is visible. The 2024 election fraud with verifiable cryptographic tally sheets (actas) is a new phenomenon: opposition had proof of fraud within hours, world acknowledged it, regime survived anyway. Colectivos as permanent parallel state replacing institutional security functions — new authoritarian tool. Oil revenue as democracy-dissolving mechanism: the resource curse operating in real time across 25 years.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; Carter Center reports; Súmate parallel count data; OCHA humanitarian data; actas database from 2024 election (opposition)

econ_conditions: Gas nationalisation 2006 — revenues funding Bono Dignidad social programmes; poverty reduction: 60% → 35% under Morales legitimising consolidation; 2019 crisis: economic stability not the issue — term limit manipulation the trigger; Arce: MAS economic continuity; 2023–24: MAS internal split (Morales vs Arce) creating parallel crisis
social: First indigenous president in Bolivia's history — Morales as Aymara coca farmer symbolic breakthrough; plurinational constitution 2009 recognising 36 indigenous nations; lowland indigenous (TIPNIS highway) vs highland indigenous tensions within MAS base; middle class mobilisation against third term (Pitita movement); evangelical church growth as new political actor
institutional: 2016 referendum: Morales lost term limit vote, Constitutional Tribunal overruled referendum — critical institutional capture; TSE (electoral court): 2019 controversy over vote count pause; OAS preliminary report alleging fraud; Constitutional Tribunal as captured institution; interim Áñez government: authoritarian overreach creating its own problems; MAS winning 2020 cleanly — Áñez arrested
political: Morales 2019: alleged fraud + OAS report + police mutiny + military 'suggesting' resignation; Áñez assuming presidency: right-wing interim overreach; 2020: Arce (MAS) winning 55% — clear mandate; Morales attempting return and challenging Arce within MAS; 2025 election: Morales barred by courts — MAS internal war continuing
external: US: NED funding anti-Morales civil society; Brazil: Lula supporting MAS return; Argentina: kirchnerismo solidarity; Cuba/Venezuela: Morales allies; OAS: 2019 report disputed — MIT study questioning it; IMF: Article IV consultations
unique_aspects: The only case where a term-limit referendum defeat (2016) was overruled by a constitutional tribunal — and where the resulting consolidation attempt then failed via street pressure + military withdrawal (2019). The OAS preliminary fraud report is analytically contested (MIT reanalysis disputed OAS conclusions) — making this the only case where the international legitimacy of a democratic removal is genuinely uncertain. Morales vs Arce MAS internal war 2023–24 shows that the 'reversal' is incomplete: the movement that was removed is now fighting itself.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; OAS 2019 report; MIT reanalysis; LAPOP; Latinobarómetro; TSE data

econ_conditions: Poorest country in Central America after Haiti; remittances 20% GDP (Nicaraguans in Costa Rica/US); Ortega: mixed economy maintaining private sector cooperation until 2018; maquila (textile) exports; 2018 crisis (-4% GDP): social security reform protest → crackdown → international isolation; sanctions limiting access to multilateral financing; Rosario Murillo (wife/VP) managing economic patronage

institutional: Supreme Electoral Council: captured; Supreme Court: packed; National Assembly: FSLN supermajority after opposition excluded; 2021 election: all viable candidates imprisoned before election; Constitutional amendments: indefinite re-election, Murillo as co-president; Catholic Church property confiscated; universities intervened
political: Ortega first era (1979–1990): Sandinista revolution; defeated 1990 (Chamorro); returned 2007 via electoral legitimacy; gradual consolidation 2007–2018 below international radar; 2018 as acceleration point; 2021: 7 presidential candidates arrested; Ortega winning with 75% — no real opponents; Murillo dynasty building: children in key positions
external: Venezuela: Petrocaribe oil subsidies (ended 2018 — economic shock); Cuba: security cooperation model; Russia: arms + diplomatic support; US: NICA Act sanctions; OAS: Nicaragua withdrew 2021; CAFTA: suspended; Costa Rica: 600,000 Nicaraguan refugees straining relations
unique_aspects: The most complete Central American authoritarian consolidation — surpassing even Somoza in institutional comprehensiveness. The Catholic Church attack is unique in LatAm: arresting a bishop (Álvarez) and expelling the papal nuncio breaks a historical LatAm norm that even Pinochet didn't cross. The Murillo co-presidency is the first formal family co-rule in Western hemisphere outside monarchies. 1,500+ NGO dissolutions in a single year exceeds Hungary's entire civil society restriction programme.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; CENIDH (human rights); Confidencial (Chamorro family media); MESENI-IACHR; OHCHR 2018 report

The peace deal rejected by referendum but implemented anyway is a unique democratic paradox — most democratic case of counter-majoritarian executive action in the dataset. Petro as former M-19 guerrilla (group that stole Bolívar's sword) winning the presidency is the most extreme political rehabilitation in LatAm — even more dramatic than Uruguay's Mujica.
data_notes: V-Dem 1900–2024; INDEPAZ conflict monitoring; UNHCR displacement data; JEP documentation; LAPOP; Verdad Abierta investigative journalism

The homicide rate reduction (-95%) is the largest in world history — making the 80,000+ arbitrary arrests politically sustainable in ways that have no historical parallel. Regional model: Honduras Xiomara Castro and Ecuador Noboa copying the security state approach — a new LatAm playbook emerging.
data_notes: V-Dem 2000–2024; InSight Crime; CRISTOSAL human rights; PDDH ombudsman; estado de excepción documentation; homicide statistics (PNC)
